editorial.headline: Marine Food Aquaculture With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers non-protected marine finfish and other seawater biota raised for consumption or as aquaculture inputs, with PMA access open nationally and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 03211 is the business of cultivating non-protected marine finfish and other seawater biota until they reach a defined age, form, or size. In practical terms, it covers the nursery, maintenance, grow-out, breeding, hatchery, and harvesting cycle for marine species that are intended either for consumption or for use as inputs in further aquaculture. The record names examples ranging from grouper, barramundi, cobia, pompano, bubara, lobster, crab, swimming crab, shellfish, oysters, squid, sea urchin, sea cucumber, and jellyfish to marine turtles, sea lions, and seals, provided the biota are not protected.

The activity is tied to seawater as the farming medium, not merely to the species list. It may take place in the sea, river estuaries, lagoons, other tidal-influenced places, and artificial facilities that use seawater for cultivation. That gives the code a broad operational shape: it can describe open marine or brackish-edge farming, as well as controlled facilities where the decisive feature is the use of seawater for marine aquaculture. The scope also expressly includes all grow-out activities for marine Pisces or finfish and all marine fish hatchery activities, which makes this a central category for food-oriented marine aquaculture rather than a narrow post-harvest or trading classification.

On business scale, the record is unusually straightforward. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators. That means the activity is not framed only for industrial-scale farms; it can also be registered by smaller operators whose activities still fall within the described cultivation, breeding, hatchery, grow-out, or harvesting scope. For foreign investment, the national position is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign stake cap in the supplied record, so the correct reading is that foreign ownership is nationally open up to full ownership for this activity.

The Bali picture is the important part, because the province applies a moratorium rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. This record, however, says KBLI 03211 is not blocked in Bali: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: a foreign investor can read this as nationally open and, on the supplied Bali data, not currently barred from PMA registration in Bali by the provincial Low and Medium-Low risk moratorium. The usual caution is not a hidden prohibition; it is simply that the registration must stay within the activity scope and the applicable risk posture shown in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is therefore clean: this marine aquaculture activity is nationally open to PMA and not currently blocked in Bali by the provincial moratorium.
